legal_resources.title: Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Woman Act, 1998
legal_resources.description: Pioneering state legislation strictly prohibiting any form of harassment of women in public spaces, educational institutions, workplaces, and public transport within Tamil Nadu.
rights: Right to safety and freedom from intimidation or harassment in public spaces and workplaces
Right to file a non-bailable FIR against perpetrators of harassment
Right to immediate police intervention and protection from All-Women Police Stations
steps: Call the 24/7 Tamil Nadu Women Helpline 181 or Emergency Helpline 112
Use the Kavalan SOS Mobile App to alert the nearest Tamil Nadu Police Control Room instantly
Approach the nearest All-Women Police Station (AWPS) to submit a written complaint
Preserve electronic or physical evidence (messages, CCTV footage, audio/video recordings)
support_organizations: Tamil Nadu State Commission for Women
Department of Social Welfare & Women Empowerment TN

legal_resources.title: Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Ragging Act, 1997
legal_resources.description: Strict state legislation prohibiting ragging in all educational institutions across Tamil Nadu, establishing mandatory suspension, dismissal, and criminal prosecution for offenders.
rights: Right of students to an environment free of physical, mental, or verbal abuse
Right to mandatory suspension and expulsion of offending students upon complaint
Right to file a criminal complaint resulting in imprisonment up to 2 years
steps: Report the incident immediately to the Anti-Ragging Committee or Principal of the institution
Submit an online complaint on the National Anti-Ragging Portal (antiragging.in)
File a complaint at the local police station if institutional action is delayed

legal_resources.title: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act (PWDVA) - TN Enforcement
legal_resources.description: Comprehensive civil law providing immediate protection orders, residence rights, maintenance, and child custody to women facing domestic abuse in Tamil Nadu.
rights: Right to reside in the shared household without illegal eviction by spouse or relatives
Right to Protection Orders prohibiting the abuser from committing violence or contacting the victim
Right to interim monetary relief, medical expenses, and emergency child custody
steps: Contact the District Protection Officer (DPO) at the District Social Welfare Office
File a Domestic Incident Report (DIR) through a registered Service Provider or All-Women Police Station
Approach the Magistrate Court for urgent ex-parte protection orders
support_organizations: District Social Welfare Protection Officers Tamil Nadu

legal_resources.title: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (POSH) Act in Tamil Nadu
legal_resources.description: Mandates Internal Committees (IC) in all workplaces with 10+ employees and Local Committees (LC) at the district level across Tamil Nadu for resolving sexual harassment complaints.
rights: Right to a safe workplace free from quid-pro-quo or hostile environment harassment
Right to submit a written complaint to the Internal Committee within 3 months of incident
Right to strict confidentiality and protection against retaliation or forced transfer during inquiry
steps: Submit a written complaint to the Internal Committee (IC) or Local Committee (LC) presiding officer
Participate in the inquiry process or request formal conciliation if desired
If workplace lacks an IC, submit the complaint directly to the District Local Committee headed by District Collector
support_organizations: Department of Labour Welfare and Skill Development TN

legal_resources.title: Equal Remuneration & Non-Discrimination Workplace Rights
legal_resources.description: Enforces equal payment of remuneration to men and women workers for same work or work of similar nature, prohibiting gender discrimination in recruitment and service conditions.
rights: Right to equal wages without gender discrimination for identical or similar work
Right against discrimination in hiring, promotions, training, or transfers based on gender
Right to claim wage differential arrears through Labor Inspectors
steps: Submit a written representation to the HR or Employer identifying wage disparity
File a claim petition before the Inspector of Labor / Conciliation Officer
Approach the Labor Court if conciliation fails
support_organizations: Department of Labour Welfare and Skill Development TN
Tamil Nadu State Legal Services Authority (TNSLSA)

legal_resources.title: Maternity Benefit Act & Tamil Nadu 12-Month Paid Leave Provisions
legal_resources.description: Provides statutory paid maternity leave, crèche facility mandates, and complete protection against dismissal during pregnancy for working women in Tamil Nadu.
rights: Right to 26 weeks paid maternity leave in private sector (12 months / 365 days paid leave for TN State Govt employees)
Right to mandatory crèche facility in establishments employing 50 or more workers
Right to work from home options post maternity leave where nature of work permits
steps: Provide formal written notice to employer regarding expected delivery date
Submit medical certificate from a registered medical practitioner
Claim full wage payment during the maternity leave period

legal_resources.title: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act in Tamil Nadu
legal_resources.description: Strict legislation protecting children under 18 years from sexual abuse, harassment, and exploitation, supported by specialized fast-track courts across Tamil Nadu.
rights: Right of every child to protection against sexual assault, harassment, and exploitation
Mandatory reporting duty for any adult aware of child abuse
Right to child-friendly recording of statement in presence of parents/guardians
steps: Call Childline 1098 or Emergency 112 immediately upon suspecting child abuse
Report to the Special Juvenile Police Unit (SJPU) or local All-Women Police Station
Child's identity remains strictly confidential by law
support_organizations: Tamil Nadu State Commission for Protection of Child Rights (TNSCPCR)

legal_resources.title: Women's Equal Property Inheritance Rights (Tamil Nadu Precedent Act)
legal_resources.description: Pioneering Tamil Nadu state amendment granting daughters equal coparcenary rights by birth in ancestral property, establishing full legal equality in family inheritance.
rights: Right to equal share in ancestral property by birth, identical to sons
Right to claim partition and demand independent share of joint family property
Right to dispose of ancestral property share by will or gift
steps: Obtain legal heir certificate and ancestral property title documents
Issue a legal notice demanding partition of property share
File a Partition Suit in the appropriate Civil Court / District Court if share is denied
support_organizations: Tamil Nadu State Legal Services Authority (TNSLSA)

legal_resources.title: Maintenance and Welfare of Senior Citizens Act - TN Enforcement
legal_resources.description: Speedy legal protection mechanism for senior citizens and elderly women to claim monthly financial maintenance and revoke property transfers made under coercion.
rights: Right to monthly financial maintenance up to ₹10,000 from adult children/heirs
Right to cancel property gift or transfer deed if children fail to provide basic care
Right to speedy disposal of maintenance applications within 90 days by RDO Tribunal
steps: Submit an application to the Senior Citizens Maintenance Tribunal headed by RDO
Attend conciliation proceedings organized by the Tribunal
Obtain a binding maintenance or property cancellation order
support_organizations: Elder Line Senior Citizen Helpline TN
legal_resources.helpline: 14567 (Elder Line National Helpline for Senior Citizens)

legal_resources.title: Free Legal Aid & Representation Services (TNSLSA Tamil Nadu)
legal_resources.description: Guarantees free legal advocate services, court fee exemption, and Lok Adalat dispute resolution for women, children, SC/ST, and low-income citizens across Tamil Nadu.
rights: Right to free legal representation by panel advocates in any civil, criminal, or family court for women
Exemption from court fees, process fees, and witness expenses
Right to resolve disputes amicably through Lok Adalats without appeal fees
steps: Visit the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) office located in District Court campus
Fill a simple free legal aid application form with identity proof
A panel advocate will be assigned by DLSA to handle your case free of charge
support_organizations: Tamil Nadu State Legal Services Authority (TNSLSA)
High Court Legal Services Committee Chennai / Madurai Bench
